$comment: The CROSS-LANGUAGE conformance vector for the AuthorizeRequest.call_sig SIGNED PAYLOAD.
frame(tool_name) || frame(agent_id), where frame(x) = u32_LITTLE_endian(len(x)) || x, all
string parts UTF-8 encoded, and context = the ASCII bytes "seam-authorize-call-v2".
The agent key then Ed25519-signs those bytes.
Every SDK MUST reproduce `payload_hex` byte-for-byte from the inputs. There is deliberately NO
bless mode: a mismatch is a CONTRACT BREAK, not a prompt to regenerate. The Rust reference is
`call_sig_payload` in seam-runtime crates/seamd/src/authorize.rs; these bytes were generated by
executing it, not transcribed from it.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Until seam-runtime #286 there was no vector for this framing — only for
the JCS digest it contains. When the runtime moved the payload from v1 (`ticket || digest`) to
v2, every published SDK kept signing v1 and nothing in either repo noticed: the SDK's own tests
passed (they verify a signature the SDK itself produced), and the break surfaced only as a live
runtime rejecting every ENFORCE call. A self-consistent signature is not a conformant one.
The v2 context tag is load-bearing: it means a v1 signature can never verify as v2, so a version
skew is a clean rejection rather than a parse ambiguity. It also means this vector's `context`
must be bumped in lockstep with any future framing change.

cases.name: all-empty
cases.why: the degenerate case — proves the context tag and five length prefixes are emitted even when every field is empty, so an implementation that 'optimizes away' empty parts diverges here

cases.name: typical
cases.why: an ordinary ENFORCE call with every field populated

cases.name: empty-agent-id
cases.why: the common case — agent_id is optional on the wire, and the empty string is signed verbatim rather than omitted

cases.name: boundary-split-a
cases.why: PAIRED WITH boundary-split-b. Concatenating without length prefixes makes ('read','x') and ('read_x','') frame identically — which would re-open the very re-pointing gap v2 closes. These two payloads MUST differ.

cases.name: utf8-and-nonprintable
cases.why: lengths are BYTE counts, not character counts — an implementation prefixing UTF-16 units or codepoints diverges on 'trans' with an umlaut and on an emoji agent_id; the ticket also carries a NUL and 0xff, which are legal bytes
